title: Clinical Decisions: Thinking Like a PCP and Owning the Call

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already follow protocols, spot life threats and decide when to move. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Use protocols and judgement, and know where one ends
  2. Think through any call in five steps
  3. Own your decisions: reassess, revise, and learn from them

Textbook: Chapter 18, PDF pages 1570–1605
slides.say: Welcome. As EMRs, you already make real decisions: you judge scene safety, spot life threats, and decide when to move. As a PCP, the number and weight of your decisions grow. You choose between protocols, decide whether to start an IV, which drug to give, and whether CPAP or a BVM is right. Each choice can help or harm, and it's yours. This chapter has no protocol of its own; it's about how you think. Today we'll cover three things: how protocols and judgement work together, a five-step way of thinking through any call, and how to own your decisions by reassessing, changing course, and learning afterwards.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎。作为 EMR，你们已经在做真正的决定：判断现场是否安全、发现生命威胁、决定何时搬运。作为 PCP，你的决定更多、分量更重：选哪个流程，要不要开静脉，给哪种药，用 CPAP 还是 BVM。每个选择都可能帮人也可能害人，而且都由你负责。本章没有对应的流程，它讲的是怎样思考。今天讲三件事：流程和判断怎样配合；一个能套用到任何出诊的五步思考法；以及怎样为自己的决定负责——再评估、改道，事后从中学习。

slides.title: Four cornerstones
slides.body:
1. Gather, evaluate, synthesize information
  2. Develop and carry out a care plan
  3. Use judgement; make independent decisions
  4. Think and work under pressure

Synthesize: fever + fast pulse + new confusion together say more than each alone.
slides.say: The book builds good practice on four cornerstones. First, gather, evaluate and synthesize information. Gathering is collecting the facts, evaluating is checking whether they're true, and synthesizing means putting them together into one picture. For example, an older patient with a fever, a fast pulse and new confusion tells you far more together than any one finding alone. Second, develop and carry out a care plan. Third, use judgement and make independent decisions when there's no time to ask. Fourth, think and work under pressure. As an EMR, the protocol often made the decision for you. As a PCP, much more of your work sits in the first and third cornerstones.
slides.sayZh: 书里把良好的院前实践建立在四块基石上。第一，收集、评估、综合信息：收集是拿到事实，评估是核实真伪，综合是把它们拼成一幅完整的图。比如一位老人发热、心跳快、又新出现意识混乱，这几条放在一起说明的远比单独任何一条多。第二，制定并执行处置计划。第三，运用判断，在来不及请示时独立决策。第四，在压力下思考和工作。当 EMR 时，常常是流程替你做了决定；作为 PCP，你更多的工作落在第一和第三块基石上。

slides.title: Protocols vs your judgement
slides.body:
Protocols and standing ordersYour judgement
Define the standard of careFills the gaps
Say what you may do without callingVague or mixed symptoms
Say when you must call firstSeveral problems at once
Built for typical patientsAlways in the patient's best interest

Spurting thigh wound: press now, tourniquet if needed. Some decisions can't wait for a call.
slides.say: Protocols and standing orders define the standard of care. They tell you what you may do without calling a physician, and when you must call first. They're your foundation, and on the BC exam you follow them closely. But the book points out their limit: they're written for typical patients. They don't cover vague symptoms, several problems at once, or a patient who needs a mix of treatments. That's where judgement comes in, always in the patient's best interest. Some decisions can't wait for a phone call: if blood is spurting from a thigh wound, you press hard right away and add a tourniquet if pressure fails. And when the situation changes, the plan changes with it.
slides.sayZh: 流程和常规医嘱规定了标准照护：哪些事不用请示医生就能做，哪些事必须先联系。它们是你的根基，BC 考试里你要严格按流程走。但书里也指出了它们的局限：它们是为典型病人写的，管不了症状含糊、多个问题并存、或需要多种处置并用的病人。这时就要靠判断，而且始终以病人的最大利益为准。有些决定等不了一通电话：大腿伤口喷血，你要立刻用力压迫，压不住就上止血带。情况一变，计划也要跟着变。

slides.title: Sick, and how sick?
slides.body:
Criticalneeds care now to surviveairway at risk, severe instability, major trauma
Seriouscare within minutes to half an houror becomes critical
Minorwalking wounded, normal vitalssmall cut, old unchanged complaint

Plus the dying or dead. The hardest decisions are the patients in the middle.
slides.say: Clear thinking starts with sorting. Critical patients need care right now to survive: an airway at risk, severe instability from bleeding, sepsis or a rhythm problem, major trauma, or a severe burn. Serious patients need care within the next few minutes to half an hour, or they'll become critical; think of multisystem trauma with stable vital signs, a COPD patient starting to tire, or mild low blood sugar with confusion. Then there are the walking wounded, with minor problems and normal vital signs, and those who are dying or dead. The book makes an honest point: the easy calls are at the two ends. The hardest decisions are the patients in the middle.
slides.sayZh: 清晰的思路从分类开始。危重病人现在就需要处置才能活：气道受威胁，失血、脓毒症或心律失常导致的严重不稳定，重大创伤，或严重烧伤。严重病人需要在接下来几分钟到半小时内处置，否则就会转为危重；比如生命体征尚稳的多系统创伤、开始疲劳的 COPD 病人、轻度低血糖伴意识混乱。另外还有问题轻微、生命体征正常、能自己走的轻伤者，以及濒死或已死亡者。书里说得很实在：两头的病人容易判断，最难的决定是夹在中间的病人。

slides.q: At a crash with several patients, which one is SERIOUS rather than CRITICAL?
options: An unresponsive driver with snoring breathing and an unprotected airway
A passenger with injuries to several body systems but fairly stable vital signs
A pedestrian with heavy bleeding and a falling blood pressure
A driver with facial burns and a hoarse voice after a car fire
slides.say: Let's check. At a crash with several patients, which one is serious rather than critical? A, an unresponsive driver with snoring breathing and an unprotected airway. B, a passenger with injuries to several body systems but fairly stable vital signs. C, a pedestrian with heavy bleeding and a falling blood pressure. D, a driver with facial burns and a hoarse voice after a car fire. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 考考你。一起多人车祸中，哪位属于「严重」而不是「危重」？A 无反应、打鼾样呼吸、气道无保护的司机；B 多个身体系统受伤、但生命体征较稳定的乘客；C 大量出血、血压下降的行人；D 车辆起火后面部烧伤、声音嘶哑的司机。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Multisystem trauma with fairly stable vital signs is serious: it needs care within minutes to half an hour, or it will become critical. A has an unprotected airway, C has severe instability from blood loss, and D suggests an airway burn or inhalation injury. All three are critical and need care right now.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。生命体征较稳定的多系统创伤属于严重：需要在几分钟到半小时内处置，否则会转为危重。A 气道无保护，C 失血导致严重不稳定，D 提示气道烧伤或吸入性损伤，这三位都属危重，现在就要处置。

slides.title: Critical thinking in five steps
slides.body:
Concept formation→Data interpretation→Application of principle
Reflection in action→Reflection on action
  • Gather: scene, appearance, LOC, history, vitals, monitors
  • Interpret: anatomy, physiology, experience; does the affect fit the story?
  • Apply: working diagnosis + differential → protocol
slides.say: The book breaks critical thinking into five steps. Concept formation is gathering everything you see, hear, smell and touch: the scene, how the patient looks, the level of consciousness, the history, the vital signs, and your tools, like the glucometer, pulse oximeter and monitor. Data interpretation is making sense of it with your anatomy, physiology and experience. Check whether the patient's affect, the emotion they show, fits their story. A woman who says she's fine but won't look at you and keeps glancing at her partner deserves another question. Application of principle means choosing a working diagnosis, keeping a differential in mind, and following the matching protocol. The last two steps are about reflection, and they come next.
slides.sayZh: 书里把批判性思维分成五步。概念形成：收集你看到、听到、闻到、摸到的一切——现场、病人的样子、意识水平、病史、生命体征，以及血糖仪、脉氧仪、监护仪等工具的结果。数据解读：用解剖、生理知识和经验去理解这些信息。要看病人的情感，也就是表现出来的情绪，和他说的是否吻合。一位女士说自己没事，却不看你、不停瞟向伴侣，就值得再多问一句。应用原则：定一个工作诊断，心里留着鉴别清单，按相应的流程处理。后两步是反思，接下来讲。

slides.title: Reassessment tests your diagnosis
slides.body:
Every reassessment tests your working diagnosis

  • Ask: did the treatment do what I expected?
  • Yes → diagnosis supported; carry on
  • No → back to your differential
  • "Asthma" not easing, crackles, swollen ankles? Think heart failure
  • Document the effect, not just the action
slides.say: Reflection in action means thinking while you work. Every reassessment is really a test of your working diagnosis. After each treatment, ask: did it do what I expected? If yes, your diagnosis gains support. If not, go back to your differential list. Here's an example. You give salbutamol to a patient you think has asthma, but the breathing doesn't improve, and now you hear crackles in both lungs and notice swollen ankles. Maybe this is heart failure, and your plan should change. That's not failure; it's good practice. In your documentation, write the effect of each treatment, not just the fact that you gave it.
slides.sayZh: 行动中反思，就是边做边想。每次再评估其实都是在检验你的工作诊断。每做一项处置都问：效果符合预期吗？符合，诊断就多了支持；不符合，就回到鉴别清单。举个例子：你以为病人是哮喘，给了沙丁胺醇，呼吸却没改善，这时又听到双肺湿啰音、发现脚踝水肿。可能是心衰，你的计划就该改。这不是失败，而是好的做法。记录时要写每项处置的效果，而不只是写你做了什么。

slides.title: Three traps
slides.body:
Tunnel visionlocking onto one ideasee little, miss a lot
Atypicalpainless neck fracture; heart attack with only fatiguee.g. women after menopause
Pertinent negativean expected finding that's missinglowers the odds, doesn't rule out

No fever doesn't rule out infection in an older adult.
slides.say: Three traps catch good paramedics. Tunnel vision means locking onto one idea: you see little and miss a lot. Atypical presentations are patients who don't follow the textbook. A neck fracture can be painless. A heart attack, especially in women after menopause, may show only sudden weakness, fatigue, dizziness or shortness of breath, with no chest pain. Pertinent negatives are findings you'd expect but don't see, like no cough and no fever in someone you think has pneumonia. A pertinent negative lowers the chance of a diagnosis, but it doesn't rule it out; older adults may not run a fever even with an infection.
slides.sayZh: 有三个陷阱常让好的 paramedic 中招。隧道视野是死盯一个想法：看得少，漏得多。不典型表现是不按教科书生病的病人：颈椎骨折可以不痛；心梗，尤其是绝经后女性，可能只有突然的乏力、疲劳、头晕或气短，没有胸痛。相关阴性是你预期会有、却没有的表现，比如你怀疑肺炎，病人却不咳嗽、不发热。相关阴性会降低某个诊断的可能，但不能排除它；老年人感染了也可能不发热。

slides.title: Thinking under stress
slides.body:
• Fight-or-flight: sharper senses, but weaker thinking
  • Fix: practise skills until they're automatic
  • CRM: anyone on the team may question or flag a problem
  • Errors grow with poor communication, workload, noise, fatigue
  • Checklist: scan, stop and think, decide, stay calm, reassess, communicate
slides.say: Big scenes trigger your fight-or-flight response. Your senses and reflexes get sharper, but your ability to think, focus and assess gets worse. The cure is mental conditioning: practise your skills until they're almost automatic, so your brain is free for decisions. Teams help too. Crew resource management, or CRM, comes from aviation: every member watches for errors, and anyone, even the most junior, can ask a question or point out a problem. Errors grow with poor communication, heavy workload, outside factors like weather and noise, and fatigue. The book's mental checklist: scan the scene, stop and think, decide and act, stay calm, reassess regularly, and communicate clearly with your team.
slides.sayZh: 大场面会触发你的战斗或逃跑反应：感官和反射更灵敏，但思考、专注和评估能力会变差。解药是心理训练：把技能练到几乎成为本能，大脑才腾得出空间做决定。团队也能帮忙。机组资源管理，简称 CRM，源自航空业：每个成员都盯着错误，任何人，哪怕资历最浅，都可以提问或指出问题。沟通不畅、工作量大、天气和噪声等外部因素、疲劳，都会让错误增多。书里的心理清单是：扫视全局、停下来想、决定并行动、保持冷静、定期再评估、和团队清楚沟通。

slides.title: On the street: the six Rs
slides.body:
1. Read the scene: it's gone once you leave
  2. Read the patient: look, talk, touch, listen
  3. React: life threats → worst case → most likely
  4. Reevaluate: did each treatment work?
  5. Revise the plan when new facts arrive
  6. Review your performance: CQI or with your partner

Book: a baseline for all; 2 sets if serious, 3+ if critical. BC exam: sets < 7 min apart if priority, < 17 if not.
slides.say: On the street, the book sums all this up as the six Rs. Read the scene, because that information disappears once you leave: the mechanism, the pill bottles, exactly where the patient was found. Read the patient: look, talk, touch and listen, and fix life threats as you find them. React: after life threats, rule the worst-case cause in or out, then look for the most likely one. Reevaluate: check whether each treatment worked. Revise the plan when new information arrives. Review your performance afterwards. For vital signs, the book says a baseline for every patient, two sets for a serious one, and three or more for a critical one. On the BC practical, timing counts: for a priority patient, seven minutes or more between sets costs marks.
slides.sayZh: 在街头，书里把这些归纳为六个 R。读现场：离开现场，这些信息就没了——受伤机制、药瓶、病人被发现的确切位置。读病人：看、问、摸、听，发现生命威胁就立即处理。反应：处理完生命威胁，先把最坏的原因确认或排除，再找最可能的原因。再评估：每项处置是否起效。修订计划：有新信息就改。复盘：事后回顾自己的表现。生命体征方面，书里说：每个病人一组基线，严重病人两组，危重病人三组以上。BC 实操考试还看时间间隔：优先转运的病人，两组之间隔七分钟或以上就要扣分。

slides.q: A confused diabetic patient has a glucose of 2.6 mmol/L. After D10W it is 6.8, but she is still confused and now has a facial droop. What is the best next step?
options: Give more D10W until she is fully alert
Revise your working diagnosis: assess for stroke with FAST-VAN, notify the hospital, transport promptly
Stay on scene 20 minutes to let the glucose work
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A confused diabetic patient has a blood glucose of two point six. You give D10W, and the glucose rises to six point eight, but she's still confused and now has a facial droop. What's the best next step? A, give more D10W until she's fully alert. B, revise your working diagnosis: assess for stroke with FAST-VAN, notify the hospital, and transport promptly. C, stay on scene for twenty minutes to let the glucose work. D, give glucagon IM as well. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位意识混乱的糖尿病病人血糖二点六。你给了 D10W，血糖升到六点八，但她仍然混乱，而且出现了口角歪斜。下一步最好怎么做？A 继续给 D10W 直到完全清醒；B 修订工作诊断：用 FAST-VAN 评估卒中，通知医院，及时转运；C 在现场等二十分钟让血糖起效；D 再加肌注胰高血糖素。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Your treatment fixed the number but not the patient, so reflection in action sends you back to your differential. A facial droop points to stroke, and the BC diabetic protocol reminds you to evaluate for stroke signs. The BC stroke protocol calls for FAST-VAN recognition, timely transport and notifying the receiving facility. A treats a glucose that is already normal. C delays care for a possible stroke. D is wrong because BC uses glucagon when you can't get IV access, and the glucose is already corrected.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。你的处置纠正了数字，却没纠正病人，行动中反思要求你回到鉴别清单。面瘫（口角歪斜）指向卒中，BC 糖尿病急症流程也提醒要评估卒中征象。BC 卒中流程要求用 FAST-VAN 识别、及时转运并通知接收医院。A 是在治疗一个已经正常的血糖；C 耽误了可能的卒中救治；D 错在 BC 只在开不了静脉时才用胰高血糖素，而且血糖已经纠正。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Scene safety, primary survey, fix life threats
  • History and a baseline set of vital signs
  • Follow the all-levels part of each protocol
  • Reassess and transport

PCP adds

  • More decisions: IV? which fluid or drug? CPAP or BVM + PEEP?
  • Many PCP steps are en route: don't delay transport
  • Check each drug against the history
  • Reassess after every intervention; IV checks q 5–15 min
  • Document the effect of each decision
slides.say: So what does this chapter mean for your daily practice? On the left is what every licence level does: scene safety, the primary survey, fixing life threats, getting a history and a baseline set of vital signs, and following the shared part of each protocol. On the right is how the PCP's thinking grows. You face more decision points: start an IV or not, which fluid or drug, CPAP or a BVM with a PEEP valve. Many BC PCP steps happen en route, so you decide what's done on scene and what waits. You check every drug against the history. You reassess after every intervention; BC asks for IV checks every five to fifteen minutes. And you document the effect of each decision.
slides.sayZh: 那么本章对你的日常执业意味着什么？左栏是所有执照级别都做的：现场安全、初级评估、处理生命威胁、采集病史和一组基线生命体征，以及执行每个流程里共同的部分。右栏是 PCP 思考的扩展。你要面对更多决策点：开不开静脉，给什么液体或药，用 CPAP 还是带 PEEP 阀的 BVM。BC 很多 PCP 步骤是在转运途中做的，所以你要决定哪些在现场做、哪些等上车。每种药都要对照病史查。每项干预后都要再评估，BC 要求静脉通路每五到十五分钟检查一次。还要记录每个决定的效果。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Dispatch info plans resources; it doesn't diagnose
  • "Just a cold": the patient's view is a clue, not a conclusion
  • A drug commits you: wrong diagnosis → wrong drug
  • Tired, hungry, distracted? The patient still comes first
  • No call is a waste of time: attitude shapes care
  • Learn to say "I was wrong": review is for learning
slides.say: Here are the new traps that come with more power. Dispatch information helps you plan resources and roles, but it's not a diagnosis. A patient who says it's just a cold may be right, or may be having a heart attack; respect their view, but trust your assessment. Remember that a drug commits you in a way oxygen doesn't: a wrong diagnosis can now mean a wrong drug. Fatigue, hunger and distraction can't be allowed to affect patient care; the patient comes right after your own and your crew's safety. Treat no call as a waste of time; a negative attitude almost always leads to worse care. And in review, learn to say I was wrong. Quality review is a chance to grow.
slides.sayZh: 能力变大，陷阱也跟着来。派单信息帮你规划资源和分工，但它不是诊断。说「只是感冒」的病人也许说对了，也许正在心梗；尊重他的看法，但要相信你自己的评估。记住，药物会把你绑定在一个诊断上，这是给氧做不到的：诊断错了，现在就可能给错药。疲劳、饥饿、分心都不能影响对病人的照护；病人的需要仅次于你自己和队友的安全。没有哪次出诊是浪费时间，消极的态度几乎必然导致更差的照护。复盘时要学会说「我错了」，质量审查是成长的机会。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book's morphine: opioid analgesia isn't on the BC exam
  • Book raises the feet in shock; BC hypovolemia: position supine
  • PCP fluids: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  • Naloxone: ventilate first; 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg IM/IV, or 4 mg IN
  • Stopping a resuscitation on scene: consult medical oversight
slides.say: A few BC points from this chapter. One of the book's examples involves a patient asking for morphine; opioid pain relief isn't on the BC licensing exam, and in BCEHS it's ACP care. When the book treats unexplained shock by its signs, it raises the feet; the BC hypovolemia protocol says to position the patient supine, and the PCP adds an IV and fluids, twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, en route or if there's a delay. The book asks whether every unconscious patient should get naloxone. In BC, you support ventilation first; the doses are point four, point four, point eight, then two milligrams IM or IV, or four milligrams intranasal. And to stop a resuscitation on scene, consult medical oversight.
slides.sayZh: 本章相关的几条 BC 要点。书里有个例子是病人要吗啡；阿片类镇痛 BC 执照考试不考，在 BCEHS 属于 ACP 的处置。书里按症状处理不明原因休克时抬高双脚；BC 低血容量流程要求病人平卧，PCP 再加上静脉通路和补液：每公斤二十毫升、最多两升、每五百毫升复评，在途中或有延误时进行。书里问是否每个昏迷者都该给纳洛酮。在 BC，先保证通气；剂量是零点四、零点四、零点八、再二毫克，肌注或静注，或四毫克鼻喷。要在现场终止复苏，须咨询医疗监督。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Protocols set the standard; your judgement covers what they can't
  2. Five steps: gather, interpret, apply, reflect in action, reflect on action
  3. Every reassessment tests your diagnosis: revise when the patient doesn't respond

Next: Chapter 19, Communications and Documentation
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: protocols set the standard of care, and your judgement covers what they can't, always in the patient's best interest. Two: think in five steps: gather, interpret, apply, reflect in action, and reflect on action. On the street, that's the six Rs. Three: every reassessment tests your working diagnosis. When the patient doesn't respond the way you expected, go back to your differential and revise the plan, and afterwards, review the call honestly. Next class, we'll look at how to pass all of this on: Chapter 19, communications and documentation. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，流程规定标准照护，流程管不到的地方靠你的判断，始终以病人最大利益为准。二，按五步思考：收集、解读、应用、行动中反思、行动后反思；在街头就是六个 R。三，每次再评估都在检验你的工作诊断；病人的反应不如预期，就回到鉴别清单、修订计划，事后诚实复盘。下节课讲怎样把这一切传递出去：第十九章，沟通与记录。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
